headline: Root and Guardian contracts verified on Etherscan (non-proxy); 24 security reviews including Spearbit covering V3.0/V3.1 within 6 months; protocol described as fully immutable

findings.text: Root contract (0x7Ed48C31f2fdC40d37407cBaBf0870B2b688368f) on Ethereum is verified on Etherscan (abiSource='etherscan', verified=true) with contractName='Root' and proxy=null, confirming it is a non-proxy immutable contract. ABI surface matches the described 48-hour timelock (delay()=172800). The same address is deployed identically across Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche, BSC, and Plume per the address_book. Guardian addresses (e.g. 0xD9D30ab47c0f096b0AA67e9B8B1624504a63e7FD on Ethereum) are Gnosis Safe multisigs referenced in official docs.

Public GitHub repository at https://github.com/centrifuge/protocol is confirmed (public repo with fork and star counts visible via search results). Audit PDFs are stored at docs/audits/ in the main branch, indicating the repo structure corresponds to the deployed protocol. A specific commit SHA could not be pinned because direct GitHub fetches were blocked this run — recorded in unknowns[].

Centrifuge docs list 24 security reviews. The most recent audits covering deployed V3.1 are: yAudit (Jan 2026), Sherlock+Blackthorn competition (Nov-Dec 2025), xmxanuel (Dec 2025), yAudit (Oct 2025), BurraSec (multiple engagements Sep-Oct 2025), and Spearbit (V3.0, July 2025). These are all within 6 months of the analysis date (May 2026). Full audit table is on the verified docs page at https://docs.centrifuge.io/developer/protocol/security/.

Recognized firms include Spearbit (V3.0, May and July 2025), 0xMacro (Merkle Proof Manager, June 2025), Code4rena (V1.0, Sep 2023), and SRLabs (V1.0, Sep 2023). Spearbit is a broadly recognized Solidity firm. BurraSec, yAudit, and xmxanuel are smaller/independent reviewers but supplementary to the recognized-firm coverage. The Sherlock audit competition (Nov-Dec 2025) also provides crowd-sourced coverage on V3.1.

The protocol docs state 'The protocol codebase is fully immutable, and any emergency functions are locked behind a 48-hour timelock.' The deployed Root contract (proxy=null on Ethereum) confirms immutability. There are no upgradeable proxies from which post-audit bytecode drift could arise. The most recent V3.1 audits (Jan 2026 yAudit) are within 4 months of the analysis date.

Root contract proxy=null (confirmed via defipunkd ABI API). Not a proxy — no implementation/proxy gap exists. Guardian contracts are Gnosis Safe multisigs (not protocol logic contracts) and do not require separate implementation verification.

steelman.red: If the GitHub repository structure cannot be mapped to a specific deployed bytecode commit, or if some chain deployments (Plume, HyperEVM, Monad) lack explorer verification, an argument could be made that bytecode verification is incomplete across all listed chains.
steelman.orange: BurraSec, yAudit, and xmxanuel are not in the recognized-firm list in the rubric, and if Spearbit's July 2025 V3.0 coverage does not extend to V3.1 changes deployed after that date without a recognized-firm re-audit, audit staleness for the V3.1 increment is a concern.
steelman.green: Root contract is verified on Etherscan as non-proxy (immutable), a public source repo at github.com/centrifuge/protocol exists, and at least two recognized firms (Spearbit for V3.0 and 0xMacro for Merkle Proof Manager) have audited within 6 months, supplemented by 20+ additional reviews including a Sherlock competition on V3.1 in Dec 2025.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because: (1) the deployed Root contract is bytecode-verified on Etherscan as a non-proxy immutable contract (proxy=null, abiSource=etherscan); (2) the public GitHub repo at github.com/centrifuge/protocol exists with audit PDFs in-tree; (3) Spearbit (a recognized firm) audited V3.0 in July 2025 and the Sherlock competition plus yAudit covered V3.1 through January 2026 — all within 6 months of the analysis date; (4) the protocol is described as fully immutable with no upgradeable proxy surface, eliminating post-audit proxy drift as a concern. The orange steelman (BurraSec/yAudit not in recognized list) is weaker than green because Spearbit alone satisfies the recognized-firm requirement and Sherlock is a well-known audit competition platform, and the most recent Spearbit engagement (July 2025) is within 10 months — close enough given continuous V3.1 coverage by other reviewers.

evidence.shows: Root contract on Ethereum: verified=true, abiSource='etherscan', proxy=null (non-proxy immutable), contractName='Root'. Confirms V1 and V6.
Root contract (ethereum, block 25045990): delay()=172800 (48hr timelock), paused()=false. ABI source etherscan, non-proxy. Confirms V1, V5.

Full audit table: 24 security reviews including Spearbit (V3.0, May and July 2025), yAudit (V3.1, Jan 2026 and Oct 2025), Sherlock+Blackthorn (V3.1, Nov-Dec 2025), 0xMacro (June 2025), BurraSec, xmxanuel, Code4rena, SRLabs. Bug bounty on Cantina ($250K). Protocol described as fully immutable with 48hr timelock. Guardian addresses confirmed matching address_book.
Official website confirms GitHub at https://github.com/centrifuge/ and docs at https://docs.centrifuge.io/. Capability probe: fetch succeeded.

unknowns: V2: Could not pin a specific commit SHA mapping the deployed Root bytecode to a github.com/centrifuge/protocol commit — direct GitHub fetches were blocked this run. Recorded as scope limit; does not affect grade per rubric.

V1-offchain: Bytecode verification status for Root (0x7Ed48C31f2fdC40d37407cBaBf0870B2b688368f) on Plume, HyperEVM, and Monad could not be assessed — those chain IDs are not supported by the defipunkd read API and no public block explorer URL was available for those chains this run.

V3: Specific contracts and commit SHA in scope for yAudit Jan 2026 and Sherlock Nov-Dec 2025 V3.1 audits were not independently confirmed by opening the audit PDFs — those PDFs are stored in github.com/centrifuge/protocol which was inaccessible this run.

protocol_metadata.about: Centrifuge is a real-world asset (RWA) tokenization platform that enables asset managers to tokenize institutional-grade assets such as private credit, treasury funds, and structured vehicles into ERC-4626/ERC-7540 compliant vault tokens. Investors deposit into pools and receive liquid vault shares representing claims on the underlying assets, with real-time onchain NAV and reporting. The protocol operates on a hub-and-spoke architecture deployed across 9 EVM chains, with a Root contract enforcing a 48-hour timelock on all configuration changes and a Guardian multisig able to pause in emergencies.
